common_name: Luna Rose Hibiscus (Compact Rose-Pink Hardy Hibiscus)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8 weeks before the last frost or set out container plants in spring in moist, fertile soil in full sun; Luna Rose rounds out the compact Luna series with a clear rose-pink bloom on the same tidy, well-branched frame bred for garden beds and large containers.

directions: Plant in moist, fertile soil in full sun, watering deeply and often through summer since this wetland-edge native wilts fast once the root zone dries out. Luna Rose opens solid rose-pink, 6-8 inch flowers with a deeper red throat, held on the same compact, sturdy 24-30 inch habit shared by the rest of the Luna series, making it useful where taller heirloom hardy hibiscus would overwhelm the bed. Bloom is continuous from mid to late summer into fall, and the plant dies back completely to the crown each winter before re-emerging late the following spring, so mark its location to avoid disturbing the dormant roots. Cut the previous year's stalks down to a few inches in late winter ahead of new growth.

common_name: Disco Belle Red Hibiscus (Dwarf Red-Flowered Perennial Hibiscus)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8 weeks before the last frost or set out container plants in spring in moist, fertile soil in full sun; Disco Belle Red is the solid scarlet-red color selection bred out of the dwarf, AAS award-winning Disco Belle strain.

directions: Plant in moist, fertile soil in full sun and keep the root zone consistently damp all season, since hardy hibiscus is naturally a wetland-edge plant that sulks quickly in dry ground. Disco Belle Red was selected from the original dwarf Disco Belle strain for uniform, saturated scarlet-red, 8-9 inch flowers on plants that stay only 18-24 inches tall, well under half the height of older hardy hibiscus lines, which suits it to foreground plantings and large containers. It flowers heavily from midsummer through fall and dies back to the ground each winter, returning reliably but late the following spring. Cut the dead stems back to a few inches above the soil in late winter before new shoots appear.

common_name: Disco Belle White Hibiscus (Dwarf White Red-Eyed Perennial Hibiscus)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8 weeks before the last frost or set out container plants in spring in moist, fertile soil in full sun; Disco Belle White is the crisp white, red-eyed color selection from the dwarf, AAS award-winning Disco Belle strain.

directions: Plant in moist, fertile soil in full sun, keeping the soil consistently moist through the growing season since this wetland-edge species wilts quickly once it dries out. Disco Belle White carries pure white, 8-9 inch flowers centered with a sharply contrasting red eye, held on the same compact 18-24 inch plant that defines the Disco Belle strain, making its dinner-plate-sized blooms sit close to eye level rather than atop tall, flopping stems. Flowering runs from midsummer into fall, and like other hardy hibiscus it dies back completely to the crown each winter, emerging late in spring. Cut the previous season's dead growth down to a few inches above the ground before new shoots break in late winter.

common_name: Disco Belle Pink Hibiscus (Dwarf Pink Red-Eyed Perennial Hibiscus)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8 weeks before the last frost or set out container plants in spring in moist, fertile soil in full sun; Disco Belle Pink is the clear pink, red-eyed color selection from the dwarf, AAS award-winning Disco Belle strain.

directions: Plant in moist, fertile soil in full sun, and water deeply through summer dry spells since hardy hibiscus is a wetland-edge species that wilts fast in parched soil. Disco Belle Pink produces clear pink, 8-9 inch flowers with a deep red central eye on the same dwarf, 18-24 inch plants bred into the Disco Belle strain, keeping its enormous blooms low and close to the foliage instead of on tall, sparse stems. It blooms heavily from midsummer through fall and, like other hardy hibiscus, dies back to the ground each winter and re-emerges late the following spring, so mark its planting spot to avoid disturbing the dormant crown. Trim the dead stalks down to a few inches above soil level in late winter.
